transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 47 min
Attendees: Maya Liu (Redwood AE), Jon Perez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Verdant Eng Lead), Carlos Mendes (Verdant SRE), Aisha Khan (Product), Evan Torres (Data Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Reviewed last week's pilot numbers: observed bursty load, tail latency spikes when concurrency hits > 64.
- Agreed to run a 4-hr steady-state to validate continuous batching improvements and new concurrency shaping.
- Action: SE will run bench, customer to share histograms, AE to update runbook and pricing impact.

Topics: steady-state run, continuous batching params, concurrency targets, queue depth shaping, KV cache hit rates, fallback routing, tracing artifacts.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, uh quick roll call just to make sure we've got the same attendees.
[00:07] Priya: yep priya here, carlos, aisha, evan on our side. thanks maya and jon.
[00:12] Jon: jon perez from redwood, i'll be driving the bench runs this week.
[00:16] Carlos: carlos here, s-r-e.
[00:20] Maya: awesome, goal for today is to orient on the runbook we drafted, align on the concurrency targets and queue shaping we'll test, and pick the steady-state windows. quick status: last week we saw average p95 latency around 230ms but spikes to 1.2s when concurrency jumped during bursts. continuous batching reduced cost but we need to validate under production-like sequence length distributions.
[00:45] Priya: yeah and to be clear our traffic is multi-tenanted, about 60% short prompts <64 tokens and 40% long form generation, so sequence length variance is the main worry. we also have occasional micro-bursts from our webhooks.
[01:10] Aisha: also timeline: execs want a recommended runbook by monday and a go/no-go for Dedicated by next wed, so we need numbers early.
[01:30] Jon: understood. so our plan - two experiments: 1) continuous batching with dynamic batch window 8ms/20ms thresholds and KV cache warmup; 2) concurrency shaping where we cap parallel requests per worker at 48/64/96 and run backpressure shaping at queue depth 200. we'll run each for 4 hours in steady-state.
[01:55] Carlos: small question: when you say queue depth 200 is that per host or per route? we've got multiple routes for QA/prod.
[02:05] Jon: good call, intended per worker process; we'll map that to your route by traffic weight in the run config. i'll include route mappings in the run artifacts.
[02:20] Evan: on histograms we have a heavy tail between 300-800 tokens for a subset of customers, i can share the JSON export.
[02:28] Priya: yes please. also we want to watch tokenization diffs — our prompt templates sometimes cause longer tokenization than expected.
[02:40] Maya: ok noted. quick note about kv cache: in our earlier run the K V cache hit rate was ~12% because the prompt templates were not normalized across calls; once normalized we often see hit rates rise to 35-40% which materially lowers compute. we'll include a normalization suggestion in the runbook.
[03:05] Carlos: any SLO impact from enabling aggressive pooling/batching? we need to be able to guarantee p99 latency for some routes.
[03:15] Jon: tradeoff — batching improves throughput and cost but can add queuing delay. for p99-sensitive routes we'll propose a two-tier policy: low-latency routes routed to a high-priority pool with small batch windows and a small concurrency cap; background routes hit the default pooling with larger batching windows.
[03:40] Priya: can you show the runbook now?
[03:44] Jon: sure i'll share screen — (screen share) — slide 3 is the run matrix: experiment A continuous-batch params, experiment B concurrency cap sweep, experiment C burst fallback to smaller model.
[04:10] [04:10] Jon: note: model fallback is a safety to keep throughput during capacity pressure; we recommend a shorter-context quantized variant for fallback (we call it 'mosaic-8q' in the doc but the transcription may say mosaic eight q).
[04:30] Priya: do you have rough cost delta estimates? execs will ask.
[04:34] Maya: yes in the runbook appendix there is a pricing impact tab — short summary: continuous batching + kv improvements could lower token compute spend by ~18-27% depending on hit rates; concurrency shaping trading latency for fewer nodes can save an additional 10-15% but may increase tail latency if misconfigured. we'll attach a live spreadsheet.
[05:05] Carlos: security/perf question: for Dedicated mode can we keep audit logs in our KMS and still get token-level cost breakdowns? we need both.
[05:15] Maya: yes Dedicated supports sending logs to your SIEM and you can enable customer-side KMS for keys; token-level accounting can be exported as anonymized usage reports. i'll include the compliance snippet.
[05:30] Priya: ok good. next i want to call out our main success criteria so we're aligned: 1) p99 under 800ms for web-critical routes, 2) steady-state throughput at 1.5x current production during peak with backpressure able to shed gracefully, and 3) cost per 1M tokens reduced by 15% or better.
[05:58] Jon: good clear criteria. we'll instrument the runs to measure p50/p95/p99, average KV hit rate, batch size distribution, queue depth over time, and node CPU/GPU utilization.
[06:20] Aisha: what tracing will you provide? we need request traces to link latency to batch decisions.
[06:28] Jon: we will supply per-request traces plus an aggregated batch trace timeline, plus a flamechart for GPU kernel utilization where available. note that some kernel-level metrics are vendor-specific and may be coarser in Dedicated.
[06:50] Evan: any chance the bench can simulate our webhook micro-bursts? ideally we want the same 30s burst every 10 minutes pattern.
[06:59] Jon: yes bench supports a custom arrival process; please include the exact burst timing in the histogram export. we'll replay it.
[07:10] [07:10] Priya: earlier you mentioned a fallback model, what's the expected difference in latency/cost when fallback kicks in?
[07:18] Jon: fallback to 'mosaic-8q' typically reduces latency by ~30% but at some quality degradation for long-context completions; cost per token is about 20-30% lower. important to test with your prompts.
[07:35] Priya: ok we'll add a sanity prompt set that stresses quality and fallback detection.
[07:42] Maya: great. schedule: we propose runs start tomorrow 2027-08-05 01:00 UTC and run through the day; SE will post artifacts for the continuous-batch test by 2027-08-06 10:00 PDT.
[08:00] Carlos: one ops ask: if queue depth hits the cap do you drop or pushback? we prefer pushback with a retry-after rather than silent drops.
[08:10] Jon: default is pushback with 429+retry-after; for critical routes we can configure synchronous fallback to the smaller model instead of pushback. we'll document both.
[08:25] Maya: going through the runbook checklist: pre-run items: shared histograms, validate tokenization, confirm route mapping, enable debug traces, set up a monitoring dashboard. any concerns?
[08:40] Evan: we'll need a temporary role for Redwood to access our staging logs — can you confirm minimum permissions?
[08:48] Maya: yes we'll request read-only log ingestion and S3 put for traces; i'll include a minimal IAM policy.
[08:58] Aisha: also please call out any required config changes to our SDK — we use a thin wrapper so we need the smallest code delta.
[09:07] Jon: minimal change: add header for 'x-kv-normalize' optional flag and a per-request hint for priority route. we'll include patch examples.
[09:25] Priya: good. on observability, can Redwood emit per-token cost estimates in the trace so we can map spend to customer-id?
[09:33] Jon: yes we'll optionally include token-cost tagging; for Dedicated we can do customer id hashing to help privacy.
[09:40] Maya: ok moving to metrics thresholds: SE will flag run if p99 exceeds 950ms for a sustained 5-minute window, or if GPU util goes above 92% for sustained 10 minutes, or if KV hit rate is below 10% when we expect >25%. agreed?
[10:00] Priya: agreed. also add an alert if batch size variance exceeds target by >25%.
[10:08] Jon: done.
[10:12] [10:12] (brief cross talk about naming conventions and doc links)
[10:30] Maya: quick Q from me — what's your expected concurrency ceiling in prod initially?
[10:35] Priya: we plan to ramp to 400 concurrent inflight requests across the cluster during peak; per worker concurrency target we think 64 is our sweet spot but that's exploratory.
[10:50] Jon: we'll sweep per-worker caps at 48/64/96 in the experiment. note that effective hardware concurrency differs by model and by quantization; we'll annotate results with GPU mem pressure.
[11:10] Carlos: one caution — our infra auto-scales nodes in response to CPU, not GPU; could that confound the results?
[11:20] Jon: yes we've seen that mismatch cause oscillations; for the runs we'll pin node count and disable autoscale on the test pool to isolate the effects.
[11:35] Maya: good catch.
[11:40] Priya: last point — procurement wants an early cost estimate for Dedicated monthly baseline if we choose to go that route. can you provide a ballpark?
[11:48] Maya: yes we'll include a proforma: baseline dedicated cluster to hit 1.5x throughput likely in the mid-five-figure monthly range depending on model; exact number after run.
[12:05] Evan: any integration concerns for our logging retention policy? we keep logs 180 days.
[12:12] Maya: redwood can respect customer retention windows; for traces we suggest a 14-day hot window and longer cold storage as needed.
[12:25] [12:25] Jon: ok i'll outline the bench steps quickly: 1) ingest histograms, 2) calibrate tokenizer, 3) spin pinned pool with specified node counts and disable autoscale, 4) run continuous-batch test for 4 hours capturing traces and batch metrics, 5) run concurrency sweep 4 hours, 6) run burst replay 2 hours, 7) summarize artifacts.
[12:55] Priya: timeline checks out. please make sure your bench emits the raw arrival stream so we can replay in our staging.
[13:05] Jon: will do.
[13:10] Maya: ok let's recap next steps out loud: jon runs the bench and posts artifacts by 2027-08-06; priya uploads histograms and sample prompts by 2027-08-05; maya sends the updated runbook + pricing sheet by 2027-08-05; schedule follow-up review on 2027-08-09. any additions?
[13:35] Priya: add that we'll validate fallback quality on the sample prompts.
[13:40] Maya: added.
[13:45] Carlos: one small ask — include a short troubleshooting cheat sheet in the runbook for ops: common failure modes and quick remedies.
[13:52] Maya: yep we'll include that.
[13:56] Aisha: thanks everyone — this was productive.
[14:00] Maya: thanks team, we'll follow up in email with the links.
